precepts.text: We heard him say, I will destroy this temple that is made with hands, and within three days I will build another made without hands. Those were the false witnesses; they overheard his teachings and lied on him.
precepts.point: Jesus answered and said unto them, Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up. Then said the Jews, Forty and six years was this temple in building, and wilt thou rear it up in three days?

note.label: We Are Born in Babylon

precepts.why:
Christ said, “Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up”, and the Jews answered, “Forty and six years was this temple in building, and wilt thou rear it up in three days?” They thought he meant the building.

At his trial the false witnesses brought it back: “We heard him say, I will destroy this temple that is made with hands, and within three days I will build another made without hands.” They had overheard his teachings, and they lied on him. He never said he would destroy the temple made with hands.

Even their lie points to the truth: another temple “made without hands.” The temple Christ spoke of raising up in three days was not stone at all. It was his own body, and that is what the rest of the scriptures read here make plain.

precepts.text: And they that passed by railed on him, wagging their heads, and saying, Ah, thou that destroyest the temple, and buildest it in three days, save thyself, and come down from the cross. This is Christ on the cross.
precepts.point: Jesus answered and said unto them, Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up. Then said the Jews, Forty and six years was this temple in building, and wilt thou rear it up in three days?

note.label: We Are Born in Babylon

precepts.why:
This is Christ on the cross. “And they that passed by railed on him, wagging their heads, and saying, Ah, thou that destroyest the temple, and buildest it in three days, Save thyself, and come down from the cross.”

They mocked him with the very words of John 2:19, still thinking he had boasted about the building in Jerusalem. But there he was, hanging on the cross: the temple he spoke of was being destroyed right in front of them, and they could not see it.

So we know Christ was talking about his body. “Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up”: they destroyed his body on the cross, and in three days he raised it up again. What the passersby railed at as a failed boast was the prophecy being fulfilled before their eyes.

precepts.text: Sir, we remember that that deceiver said, while he was yet alive, After three days I will rise again. So that is what he meant when he said in three days I will rebuild this temple.
precepts.point: Jesus answered and said unto them, Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up. Then said the Jews, Forty and six years was this temple in building, and wilt thou rear it up in three days?

note.label: We Are Born in Babylon

precepts.why:
After the crucifixion the chief priests and Pharisees came to Pilate, “Saying, Sir, we remember that that deceiver said, while he was yet alive, After three days I will rise again.”

They called him a deceiver, but they remembered exactly what he said, and they understood it: after three days I will rise again. That was what he meant when he said in three days I will rebuild this temple.

They had heard him teach it. So when they put up false witnesses saying he would destroy the temple and build it back, they were lying on him, twisting his words about the building, while among themselves they knew he spoke of rising from the dead. The temple raised up in three days is his body raised the third day.

precepts.text: From that time forth began Jesus to shew unto his disciples, how that he must go unto Jerusalem, and suffer many things of the elders and chief priests and scribes, and be killed, and be raised again the third day. He was talking about raising up himself the third day: Christ's body was the temple, and his temple today is us.
precepts.point: Jesus answered and said unto them, Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up. Then said the Jews, Forty and six years was this temple in building, and wilt thou rear it up in three days?

note.label: We Are Born in Babylon

precepts.why:
This is what he actually said: “From that time forth began Jesus to shew unto his disciples, how that he must go unto Jerusalem, and suffer many things of the elders and chief priests and scribes, and be killed, and be raised again the third day.” He was talking about raising up himself the third day. Christ's body was the temple.

And his temple today is us. Peter says, “Ye also, as lively stones, are built up a spiritual house, an holy priesthood, to offer up spiritual sacrifices, acceptable to God by Jesus Christ.” That's the real temple: wherever our people are gathered is a spiritual house. Lively means the laws percolate within us, with zeal, passion and fire, not a boring spirit. Paul says, “In whom all the building fitly framed together groweth unto an holy temple in the Lord”: stones have to come together, so play your position and don't try to change it through deceit. And “Know ye not that ye are the temple of God, and that the Spirit of God dwelleth in you?” “for the temple of God is holy, which temple ye are”.

How does that temple grow? “Wherefore laying aside all malice, and all guile, and hypocrisies, and envies, and all evil speakings, As newborn babes, desire the sincere milk of the word, that ye may grow thereby”. Everybody forgets verse one: you have to put away malice, deceit, jealousies and murmuring first. The sincere milk of the word is the law, and we have to drink it like a baby drinks milk, not once a month or once a week, but constantly. That is why we have to change the way we conduct ourselves and our communications: we are the temple.

precepts.text: Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up. They thought he meant the building of forty six years; but he spake of the temple of his body. His body was the greater and more perfect tabernacle, not made with hands.
precepts.point: The feast of tabernacles, seven days unto the Lord. Tabernacle, sukkot, booth: it means to dwell.

note.label: 70 Times 7: The Perfection of Mercy Through Christ

precepts.why:
“Jesus answered and said unto them, Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up.” The Jews took him simply: “Forty and six years was this temple in building, and wilt thou rear it up in three days?” They thought he meant the building.

“But he spake of the temple of his body.” His body is the temple, the tabernacle. Hebrews 9:11 shows it: “But Christ being come an high priest of good things to come, by a greater and more perfect tabernacle, not made with hands, that is to say, not of this building”. His body was that greater and more perfect tabernacle. “Neither by the blood of goats and calves, but by his own blood he entered in once into the holy place, having obtained eternal redemption for us.”

So the booths Israel dwelt in for the feast of tabernacles point to Christ’s own body, the true tabernacle in which God dwelt among us, destroyed and raised up again in three days.

precepts.text: For the zeal of thine house hath eaten me up.
precepts.point: His disciples remembered that it was written, The zeal of thine house hath eaten me up. He was fulfilling what David had written.

note.label: John 2: The First Miracle and the Cleansing of the Temple

precepts.why:
David wrote it: “For the zeal of thine house hath eaten me up; and the reproaches of them that reproached thee are fallen upon me.” When Christ made a scourge of small cords and drove them all out of the temple, with the sheep and the oxen, poured out the changers' money and overthrew the tables, his disciples remembered that it was written, “The zeal of thine house hath eaten me up.”

He was fulfilling what David had written. He drove grown men out with a whip, and said unto them that sold doves, “Take these things hence; make not my Father’s house an house of merchandise.” No man had business trading in there at the passover. That is the zeal of his Father's house eating him up, exactly as the psalm says.

precepts.text: For the Jews require a sign, and the Greeks seek after wisdom.
precepts.point: The saying was kept and used against him later by false witnesses at his trial.

note.label: John 2: The First Miracle and the Cleansing of the Temple

precepts.why:
The Jews answered him, “What sign shewest thou unto us, seeing that thou doest these things?” Asking after signs was their habit, and the epistle names it: “For the Jews require a sign, and the Greeks seek after wisdom”.

That is why they came at him with that question after he cleansed the temple. The Jews require a sign. Paul knew his people, and that is the very thing we see them doing here.

precepts.text: The same sign given in other words: as Jonas was three days and three nights in the whale's belly.
precepts.point: The saying was kept and used against him later by false witnesses at his trial.

note.label: John 2: The First Miracle and the Cleansing of the Temple

precepts.why:
The scribes and Pharisees asked the same thing: “Master, we would see a sign from thee.” Christ answered, “An evil and adulterous generation seeketh after a sign; and there shall no sign be given to it, but the sign of the prophet Jonas: For as Jonas was three days and three nights in the whale’s belly; so shall the Son of man be three days and three nights in the heart of the earth.”

That is the same sign given in other words. In John 2 he said, “Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up.” In Matthew, as Jonas was three days and three nights in the whale's belly, so shall the Son of man be three days and three nights in the heart of the earth. Both are the sign of his death and his rising the third day, the one sign that generation would be given.

precepts.text: Him God raised up the third day, and shewed him openly.
precepts.point: The saying was kept and used against him later by false witnesses at his trial.

note.label: John 2: The First Miracle and the Cleansing of the Temple

precepts.why:
“Him God raised up the third day, and shewed him openly”. That is the sign fulfilled. He said, “Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up”, and God raised him up the third day and shewed him openly.

“When therefore he was risen from the dead, his disciples remembered that he had said this unto them; and they believed the scripture, and the word which Jesus had said.” Peter, in Acts, is one of those disciples telling it after it came to pass.

precepts.text: Howbeit the most High dwelleth not in temples made with hands.
precepts.point: The saying was kept and used against him later by false witnesses at his trial.

note.label: John 2: The First Miracle and the Cleansing of the Temple

precepts.why:
“But he spake of the temple of his body.” It went over their heads, and they answered with the “Forty and six years” the temple was in building. But Stephen says, “Howbeit the most High dwelleth not in temples made with hands; as saith the prophet”.

The Most High does not dwell in temples made with hands. So the temple Christ spoke of was not the building of stone that took forty and six years. It was his body.

precepts.text: Know ye not that your body is the temple of the Holy Ghost which is in you?
precepts.point: The saying was kept and used against him later by false witnesses at his trial.

note.label: John 2: The First Miracle and the Cleansing of the Temple

precepts.why:
The body itself is called a temple in the scriptures: “What? know ye not that your body is the temple of the Holy Ghost which is in you, which ye have of God, and ye are not your own?”

If our body is the temple of the Holy Ghost, then Christ's own words, “Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up”, are plain. He spake of the temple of his body, the way Paul speaks of the body as a temple.

precepts.text: They sought false witness, and at the last two came saying, This fellow said, I am able to destroy the temple of God.
precepts.point: The saying was kept and used against him later by false witnesses at his trial.

note.label: John 2: The First Miracle and the Cleansing of the Temple

precepts.why:
The saying was kept and used against him later by false witnesses at his trial. “Now the chief priests, and elders, and all the council, sought false witness against Jesus, to put him to death; But found none: yea, though many false witnesses came, yet found they none. At the last came two false witnesses, And said, This fellow said, I am able to destroy the temple of God, and to build it in three days.”

They twisted it. He said, “Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up”, speaking of the temple of his body; they made it, I am able to destroy the temple of God. They never understood the sign they asked for, and in the end they sought false witness with it to put him to death.

precepts.text: Peter shews that David spake of the resurrection of Christ, for David is dead and buried and his sepulchre is with us unto this day.
precepts.point: The saying was kept and used against him later by false witnesses at his trial.

note.label: John 2: The First Miracle and the Cleansing of the Temple

precepts.why:
Peter shews that David spake of the resurrection of Christ. “For David speaketh concerning him, I foresaw the Lord always before my face, for he is on my right hand, that I should not be moved: Therefore did my heart rejoice, and my tongue was glad; moreover also my flesh shall rest in hope: Because thou wilt not leave my soul in hell, neither wilt thou suffer thine Holy One to see corruption.”

Then Peter tells them plainly that David was not speaking of himself: “let me freely speak unto you of the patriarch David, that he is both dead and buried, and his sepulchre is with us unto this day.” David is dead and buried, and his sepulchre is with us unto this day. “Therefore being a prophet, and knowing that God had sworn with an oath to him, that of the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh, he would raise up Christ to sit on his throne; He seeing this before spake of the resurrection of Christ, that his soul was not left in hell, neither his flesh did see corruption.”

That is the scripture his disciples believed when he was risen from the dead: “they believed the scripture, and the word which Jesus had said.” David had written of the resurrection, and Christ had said, “in three days I will raise it up.” Both came to pass.

precepts.text: Jesus knowing their thoughts said, Wherefore think ye evil in your hearts?
precepts.point: Many believed when they saw the miracles, but he did not commit himself unto them, for he knew all men, and needed not that any should testify of man: for he knew what was in man.

note.label: John 2: The First Miracle and the Cleansing of the Temple

precepts.why:
Many believed in his name when they saw the miracles which he did, but Jesus did not commit himself unto them, “because he knew all men, And needed not that any should testify of man: for he knew what was in man.” Matthew shows that in action: “And Jesus knowing their thoughts said, Wherefore think ye evil in your hearts?”

He knew their thoughts. Nobody had to tell him what a man was thinking; he knew what was in man, and he answered the evil in their hearts before they spoke it. That is why he did not commit himself to the many who believed only because of the miracles.

precepts.text: Destroy this temple and in three days I will raise it up, Christ's resurrection foreshadowing Israel's revival.
precepts.point: The vision was done three times, symbolizing Israel being revived and raised up the third day.

note.label: Acts 11: The Gentiles Are Scattered Israel

precepts.why:
“Jesus answered and said unto them, Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up.”

Christ's resurrection on the third day foreshadows Israel's revival. As he was raised up in three days, Israel is raised up the third day, and that is what the vision done three times shows.
